headline: Chips are dragging NQ −0.9% to 28,317 while the Dow and small caps keep rallying. Lean SHORT at the open below the overnight midpoint ~28,418; flip LONG on a reclaim of 28,450, add on a break of the 28,167.75 overnight low.
session_note: Cash open 9:30 AM ET (10:30 AM Atlantic) · morning window · Fed's Hammack 8:50 and Barkin 9:10 AM ET · NFP Friday

flip.long: LONG if NQ reclaims and holds 28,450 (above the overnight midpoint ~28,418, ≈ NDX 28,290, back above Wednesday's NDX low 28,276), meaning the megacap bid is outweighing the chip selling. Target Wednesday's settle 28,566.75.
flip.short: SHORT stays on while NQ is below ~28,418. Stronger below the overnight low 28,167.75 (≈ NDX 28,038); next target the 28,038 area, Tuesday's NQ low.

thesis: A low-conviction lean **SHORT** for the open. **NQ is −249.5 pts / −0.87% at 28,317.25 (8:35 AM ET)** after Wednesday's 1.4% Nasdaq rally, and it sits in the lower half of a 28,167.75–28,668.50 overnight range [1]. The rotation away from tech is speeding up: Dow futures are +0.6%, Russell +0.6% and S&P +0.2% while Nasdaq lags [2,3]. The weight is in semis: **Qualcomm is −10.7%** after missing on Q4 smartphone chip sales and Apple revenue, AMD −4.8%, AVGO −2.5% and NVDA −1.4%, as UBS warns data-center pauses after the Democratic sweep put ~30% of 2028 additions at risk [2,4]. Megacaps are the offset: AMZN +2%, AAPL +1.2%, GOOGL +1.2% and META +0.9% premarket [4]. Labor data stays hot: **jobless claims fell to 189K vs 196K expected** after Wednesday's ADP beat, and **December hike odds are ~82%** [5,6]. The 10-year is flat at ~4.90%, the dollar is +0.1% at 101.6, and oil is bouncing (WTI +1.6% at ~$89.5) [7]. On Wednesday's ~130-pt futures premium, that implies a cash open near **~28,190, below Wednesday's NDX low of 28,276** [1]. So **lean short below ~28,418; flip long above 28,450**.

bullets.text: NQ is −0.87% at 28,317.25, in the lower half of its 28,167.75–28,668.50 overnight range [1]. The implied ~28,190 cash open is below Wednesday's NDX low. That's an estimate, not a quote.

bullets.text: Qualcomm −10.7% on its Q4 handset-chip miss, AMD −4.8%, AVGO −2.5%, NVDA −1.4%, Marvell and Intel lower, and data-center names are down on fears of state-level pauses after the Democratic sweep [2,4].

bullets.label: Bull case:
bullets.text: AMZN, AAPL, GOOGL and META are all up 1–2% premarket, with UBS arguing a slower AI buildout helps the platforms and that semis are near multi-year-low valuations [2,4]. VIX is near 16.8 after its biggest one-day drop since April 2025, and the 10-year is under 4.90–4.91% [3,7]. A dip toward the overnight low could get bought.

bullets.label: Bear case:
bullets.text: Chips are leading lower for a second day, oil is bouncing, and the labor data keeps pushing hike odds up ahead of Friday's payrolls. A hawkish Hammack or Barkin could add to it.

bullets.text: NQ reclaims and holds 28,450 (above the overnight midpoint, ≈ NDX 28,290) in the first 30 minutes. Target Wednesday's settle 28,566.75.

data_notes: NQ and stock quotes are from Yahoo and may be delayed ~10 min. Yahoo's NQ 'previous close' field showed 28,127.50, which doesn't match its own Nov 4 daily bar (28,566.75); I used the daily bar as Wednesday's settle, so the % change is −0.87% here vs −0.5% to −0.7% in earlier news reports. The implied NDX open uses Wednesday's ~130-pt premium (NQ settle 28,566.75 vs NDX close 28,437.17) and is an estimate; NDX-equivalent levels use the same basis. Jobless claims consensus differs by source (196K FX Blue/Helious vs 212K Econoday); it's a beat either way. Productivity and unit labor costs (8:30 AM) actuals weren't found. Fed odds are CME FedWatch as reported by FXStreet; the CME page itself wasn't read.
